text: APA in-text citation should use author-date form and distinguish narrative citation from parenthetical citation.
Publication years should be placed in parentheses when required by APA citation syntax.
Every empirical or quantitative claim should be attached to a specific and verifiable source.
GB/T numbered references should correspond to complete bibliography entries with author title year and source type.
Citation feedback should evaluate whether a reader can trace a claim to a concrete source.
A single broad citation at the end of a paragraph should not hide multiple unsupported literature claims.
An abstract should state problem objective method evaluation result and contribution in a coherent sequence.
Abstract elements are weak when solution and implementation details appear before the research problem and objective.
An introduction should move from background to problem to research gap before presenting the contribution.
The contribution statement should answer the identified research gap rather than only list product features.
IMRAD writing should keep method procedure separate from results and discussion interpretation.
Result claims should appear in the results section rather than inside the method description.
The results section should report measured experimental outcomes instead of repeating interface design details.
Evaluation results should include metrics such as node existence rate threshold pass rate and feedback completion.
A conclusion should synthesize established findings and avoid introducing new unsupported claims.
Limitations should state what the study cannot prove and define boundaries for interpretation.
A background paragraph should establish the educational or research context before technical implementation details.
Paragraphs should sequence context problem and technical response so readers understand why the design is needed.
A method paragraph should describe data procedure configuration and metrics so another researcher can reproduce the study.
A result paragraph should report measured findings with numbers comparisons and concise interpretation.
A paragraph should use a clear topic sentence and keep sentence roles aligned with its main function.
A discussion paragraph should interpret findings rather than merely repeat numerical results.
Discussion should explain mechanisms implications and constraints without inventing new experimental data.
A limitation paragraph should clearly state evidence boundaries and future work instead of promotional claims.
A claim should be connected to evidence and reasoning so readers can follow the argument chain.
Evidence is weakly integrated when the paragraph lists findings without explaining how they support the claim.
Literature evidence should be synthesized by comparing findings rather than stacking unrelated citations.
Paraphrased evidence should preserve the source meaning and avoid unsupported generalization.
Academic claims should use cautious language when evidence is limited or context dependent.
Academic writing should avoid promotional language and keep evaluative claims evidence bound.
